summary: Which statues are forbidden as idols? Rabbi Meir says all of them; the Sages say only ones holding special things in their hand.

chunks.en: All statues are forbidden,
chunks.st: All statues are forbidden,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is prohibited to derive benefit from them,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן נֶעֱבָדִין פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה,
chunks.en: because they are worshipped once a year.
chunks.st: because they are worshipped at least once a year;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא כָל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ
chunks.en: the only one forbidden is one that has in its hand
chunks.st: The only type of statue that is forbidden is any statue that has in its hand

chunks.en: a stick, or a bird, or a ball.
chunks.st: a staff, or a bird, or an orb,
chunks.stMore: as these are indications that this statue is designated for idolatry. If the statue is holding a different item, it may be assumed that the statue was fashioned for ornamental purposes and not for worship.

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: any statue that has anything at all in its hand.
chunks.st: It is prohibited to derive benefit even from any statue that has any item whatsoever in its hand.

summary: Broken pieces of statues are allowed. But the shape of a hand or a foot is forbidden, because people worship things like that.

chunks.en: One who finds broken pieces of statues,
chunks.st: In the case of one who finds unidentifiable fragments of statues,

chunks.en: they are allowed.
chunks.st: these are permitted,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one may derive benefit from them.

chunks.he: מָצָא תַבְנִית יָד אוֹ תַבְנִית רֶגֶל,
chunks.en: If he found the shape of a hand or the shape of a foot,
chunks.st: If one found an object in the figure of a hand or in the figure of a foot,

chunks.en: they are forbidden,
chunks.st: these are forbidden,

chunks.en: because things like them are worshipped.
chunks.st: as objects similar to those are worshipped.

summary: Vessels with pictures of the sun, moon or a dragon must be thrown into the Dead Sea. The Sages also argue with Rabbi Yosei about grinding up an idol, because even its dust may not be used.

chunks.en: One who finds vessels with a picture of the sun on them,
chunks.st: In the case of one who finds vessels, and upon them is a figure of the sun,

chunks.en: a picture of the moon,
chunks.st: a figure of the moon,

chunks.en: a picture of a dragon,
chunks.st: or a figure of a dragon,

chunks.en: must take them to the Dead Sea.
chunks.st: he must take them and cast them into the Dead Sea
chunks.stMore: and not derive any benefit from them, as they are assumed to be objects of idol worship.

words.note: The Dead Sea, a salty sea where things are lost forever.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: those on fancy vessels are forbidden.
chunks.st: Those figures that are upon respectable vessels are forbidden.

chunks.en: Those on lowly vessels are allowed.
chunks.st: Those that are upon disgraceful vessels are permitted.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.he: שׁוֹחֵק וְזוֹרֶה לָרוּחַ אוֹ מַטִּיל לַיָּם.
chunks.en: he grinds it up and throws it to the wind or into the sea.
chunks.explain: This is how to get rid of an idol.
chunks.st: When one encounters an idol, he should grind the idol and throw the dust to the wind or cast it into the sea.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him: What is the good of that?

chunks.en: even that becomes fertilizer,
chunks.explain: So a Jew would still get use from the idol.
chunks.st: That also gives a Jew benefit from the idol, as it becomes fertilizer for his crops,

words.note: Stuff that helps plants grow.

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "And nothing shall stick
chunks.st: and deriving any kind of benefit is prohibited, as it is stated: “And nothing of the proscribed items shall cleave

chunks.en: to your hand from the forbidden things."
chunks.st: to your hand” (Deuteronomy 13:18).

summary: A non-Jew asked Rabban Gamliel how he could bathe in a bathhouse that had a statue of the idol Aphrodite. Rabban Gamliel answered that the statue was only a decoration for the bathhouse, and people do not treat it like a god.

chunks.en: Proklos ben Plospos asked
chunks.st: A wise gentile, Proclus ben Plospus, once asked a question

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel in Akko,
chunks.st: of Rabban Gamliel in the city of Akko

chunks.en: while he was bathing in the bathhouse of Aphrodite.
chunks.st: when he was bathing in the bathhouse of the Greek god Aphrodite.

words.note: A Greek idol.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Proclus said to him:

chunks.en: It is written in your Torah,
chunks.st: It is written in your Torah:

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה מִן הַחֵרֶם.
chunks.en: "And nothing from the forbidden things shall stick to your hand."
chunks.st: “And nothing of the proscribed items shall cleave to your hand” (Deuteronomy 13:18).

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה רוֹחֵץ בַּמֶּרְחָץ שֶׁל אַפְרוֹדִיטִי.
chunks.en: Why are you bathing in the bathhouse of Aphrodite?
chunks.st: For what reason do you bathe before an idol in the bathhouse of Aphrodite?

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said to him:

chunks.st: One may not answer questions related to Torah in the bathhouse.

chunks.en: And when he came out, he said to him,
chunks.st: And when he left the bathhouse, Rabban Gamliel gave him several answers. He said to him:

chunks.en: I did not come into her space,
chunks.st: I did not come into its domain;

chunks.en: she came into my space.
chunks.explain: The bathhouse was there before the statue.
chunks.st: it came into my domain.
chunks.stMore: The bathhouse existed before the statue dedicated to Aphrodite was erected.

chunks.en: People do not say,
chunks.st: Furthermore, people do not say:

chunks.en: "Let's make a bathhouse to decorate Aphrodite,"
chunks.st: Let us make a bathhouse as an adornment for Aphrodite;

chunks.en: but they say,
chunks.st: rather, they say:

chunks.en: "Let's make an Aphrodite to decorate the bathhouse."
chunks.st: Let us make a statue of Aphrodite as an adornment for the bathhouse.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, the main structure is not the Aphrodite statue, but the bathhouse.

chunks.en: Another answer:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel continued: Alternatively, there is another answer:

chunks.en: even if they gave you a lot of money,
chunks.st: Even if people would give you a lot of money,

chunks.he: אִי אַתָּה נִכְנָס לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלְּךָ
chunks.en: you would not go in front of your avodah zarah
chunks.st: you would not enter before your object of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: without clothes, or tamei, or doing something not nice in front of it.
chunks.st: naked, or as one who experienced a seminal emission who comes to the bathhouse to purify himself, nor would you urinate before it.

words.note: A kind of tumah.

chunks.en: But this statue stands at the opening of the drain pipe,
chunks.st: This statue stands upon the sewage pipe

chunks.en: and all the people do things that are not nice in front of it.
chunks.st: and all the people urinate before it.

chunks.en: The Torah only says "their gods."
chunks.st: There is no prohibition in this case, as it is stated in the verse only: “Their gods” (see Deuteronomy 12:2),

chunks.he: אֶת שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֱלוֹהַּ, אָסוּר.
chunks.en: Something they treat like a god is forbidden.
chunks.st: which indicates that a statue that people treat as a deity is forbidden,

chunks.he: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֱלוֹהַּ, מֻתָּר:
chunks.en: And something they do not treat like a god is allowed.
chunks.st: but one that people do not treat with the respect that is due to a deity is permitted.

summary: If non-Jews worship mountains and hills, the mountains are allowed, but things put on them are forbidden. An ashera tree is forbidden because people planted or shaped it.

chunks.he: הַגּוֹיִם הָעוֹבְדִים אֶת הֶהָרִים וְאֶת הַגְּבָעוֹת,
chunks.en: The non-Jews who worship the mountains and the hills,
chunks.st: With regard to the halakha in the case of the gentiles who worship the mountains and the hills,

chunks.en: the mountains are allowed, but what is on them is forbidden,
chunks.st: the mountains and hills are permitted, but what is upon them is forbidden.
chunks.stMore: It is not prohibited to derive benefit from the mountains and hills themselves, and they can be used for planting, harvesting, and the like. But if gentiles coated them with gold or silver, it is prohibited to derive benefit from the coating,

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "Do not want
chunks.st: as it is stated: “The graven images of their gods shall you burn with fire; you shall not covet

chunks.en: the silver and gold on them and take it."
chunks.st: the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself,
chunks.stMore: lest you be snared by it; for it is an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 7:25).

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says
chunks.stMore: with regard to the verse: “You shall destroy all the places where the nations that you are to dispossess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every leafy tree” (Deuteronomy 12:2):

chunks.en: "their gods on the mountains" —
chunks.st: The mitzva to destroy objects of idol worship applies to “their gods, upon the high mountains,”

chunks.en: but not the mountains as their gods.
chunks.st: but not to the mountains themselves that are their gods.

chunks.en: "their gods on the hills" —
chunks.st: Similarly it applies to “their gods…upon the hills,”

chunks.en: but not the hills as their gods.
chunks.st: but not to the hills themselves that are their gods.

chunks.en: Then why is an ashera forbidden?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: And for what reason, then, is an ashera forbidden?
chunks.stMore: Doesn’t the verse also state: “And under every leafy tree,” which indicates that the mitzva to destroy objects of idol worship does not apply to the trees themselves?

words.note: A tree that people worship as an idol.

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ תְּפִיסַת יָד אָדָם,
chunks.en: Because people worked on it with their hands,
chunks.st: The mishna answers: It is because it is the product of human involvement and did not grow by itself,

chunks.he: וְכֹל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ תְּפִיסַת יְדֵי אָדָם אָסוּר.
chunks.en: and anything that people worked on with their hands is forbidden.
chunks.st: and the halakha is that anything that is the product of human involvement is forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: I will explain and decide it for you.
chunks.st: I will explain and decide the matter before you.
chunks.stMore: The verse does not indicate limitations to the halakhic definition of idols; rather, it is simply giving indicators of prevalent idolatrous practice:

chunks.en: Any place where you find
chunks.st: Everywhere that you find

chunks.he: הַר גָּבוֹהַּ וְגִבְעָה נִשָּׂאָה וְעֵץ רַעֲנָן,
chunks.en: a tall mountain, a high hill, or a leafy tree,
chunks.st: a high mountain, or an elevated hill, or a leafy tree,

chunks.en: know that there is avodah zarah there.
chunks.st: know that there is idol worship there.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

summary: If a wall shared with a house of idol worship falls, a Jew may not rebuild it in the same place. The stones of a house of idol worship make a person tamei.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בֵיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְנָפַל,
chunks.en: If someone's house was next to a house of avodah zarah and the wall fell,
chunks.st: In the case of one whose house was adjacent to a house of idol worship and the dividing wall fell,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is forbidden to build it again.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to rebuild it.

chunks.en: What should he do?
chunks.st: What should he do?

chunks.he: כּוֹנֵס בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּבוֹנֶה.
chunks.en: He moves four amos into his own land and builds.
chunks.st: He should withdraw into his own property four cubits and build the wall there.
chunks.stMore: In talmudic times, external walls to homes were often built in two parts, with a functional space between them.

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm.

chunks.en: If the wall's space was his and the avodah zarah's,
chunks.st: If the space between the two parts of the wall belonged to him and to the house of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is judged half and half.
chunks.st: the area is treated as half and half
chunks.stMore: with regard to withdrawing into his property before rebuilding the wall; he may build the wall four cubits from the middle of that space.

chunks.en: Its stones, its wood and its dust
chunks.st: The stones of the fallen wall, its wood, and its dust,

chunks.en: make tamei like a sheretz,
chunks.st: transmit impurity like a creeping animal,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one who touches them becomes impure like one who touches a creeping animal,

words.note: A small crawling animal that makes things tamei.

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "You shall find it disgusting."
chunks.explain: The Torah uses a word like sheretz.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and be accursed like it; you shall detest it [shakketz teshakketzennu],
chunks.stMore: and you shall abhor it; for it is a proscribed item” (Deuteronomy 7:26). The term shakketz is used in a different form, shekketz, with regard to creeping animals.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: כַּנִּדָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה ל) תִּזְרֵם כְּמוֹ דָוָה,
chunks.en: like a niddah, as it says: "Throw them away like something tamei,
chunks.st: Those items transmit impurity like a menstruating woman, as it is stated: “You will put them far away as a menstruating woman;

A book of the Navi.

chunks.en: say to it: Go away!"
chunks.st: you shall say to it: Go away” (Isaiah 30:22).

chunks.en: Just as a niddah makes tamei by carrying,
chunks.st: Just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity by carrying,
chunks.stMore: as one who moves a menstruating woman, even without touching her, becomes impure,

chunks.en: so too avodah zarah makes tamei by carrying.
chunks.st: so too, objects of idol worship transmit impurity by carrying.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

summary: There are three kinds of houses, three kinds of stones, and three kinds of ashera trees: some are forbidden forever, and some become allowed. The mishnah also tells a story of Rabbi Shimon and a worshipped tree.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of houses.
chunks.st: With regard to idol worship there are three types of houses, each with its own halakhot.

chunks.en: A house built from the start for avodah zarah
chunks.st: A house that one built initially for the purpose of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is prohibited to derive benefit from such a house.

chunks.en: If he plastered it and painted it for avodah zarah, and added something new,
chunks.st: If one plastered a house or cemented it for the purpose of idol worship, and he thereby added a layer to the walls of the house,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what he added.
chunks.st: one removes that which he added,
chunks.stMore: and the rest of the house is permitted.

chunks.en: If he brought avodah zarah into it and took it out,
chunks.st: If one brought an object of idol worship into a house temporarily and then removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the house is then permitted.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of stones.
chunks.st: With regard to idol worship there are three types of stones, each with its own halakhot.

chunks.en: A stone that was cut from the start for an idol's stand
chunks.st: A stone that one initially hewed for use in a platform [bimos] for an idol

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden.

chunks.he: סִיְּדָהּ וְכִיְּרָהּ לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְחִדֵּשׁ,
chunks.en: If he plastered it and painted it for avodah zarah, and added something new,
chunks.st: If one plastered a stone or cemented it for the sake of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what he added.
chunks.st: one removes that which he plastered or cemented and the stone is permitted.

chunks.en: If he stood avodah zarah on it and removed it,
chunks.st: If one erected an object of idol worship upon a stone and subsequently removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: the stone is then permitted.

chunks.en: There are three kinds of ashera trees.
chunks.st: There are three types of trees that were used as part of idolatrous rites [ashera]:

words.note: Trees that are worshipped as idols.

chunks.he: אִילָן שֶׁנְּטָעוֹ מִתְּחִלָּה לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: A tree planted from the start for avodah zarah
chunks.st: A tree that one initially planted for the sake of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden,
chunks.stMore: and one may not derive benefit from any part of the tree.

chunks.he: גִּדְּעוֹ וּפִסְּלוֹ לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהֶחֱלִיף,
chunks.en: If he cut it down or trimmed it for avodah zarah, and it grew back,
chunks.st: If one lopped off part of the trunk of a tree or trimmed its branches for the sake of idol worship, i.e., to worship that which would regrow there, and the tree’s trunk or limbs regrew,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: he takes off what grew back.
chunks.st: one removes that which has regrown
chunks.stMore: and burn it. The remainder of the tree is then permitted.

chunks.en: If he stood avodah zarah under it and then removed it,
chunks.st: If one erected an object of idol worship beneath a tree and subsequently removed it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: it is permitted to derive benefit from the tree.

chunks.en: Which tree is an ashera?
chunks.st: Which tree is deemed forbidden as an ashera?

chunks.en: Any tree that has avodah zarah under it.
chunks.st: Any tree that has an object of idol worship beneath it.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: any tree that people worship.
chunks.st: Any tree that people worship.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְצַיְדָּן בְּאִילָן שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְדִין אוֹתוֹ,
chunks.en: And there was a story in Tzaidan about a tree that people worshipped,
chunks.st: And there was an incident in Tzaidan involving a tree that people would worship,

words.note: A city.

chunks.en: and they found a pile of stones under it.
chunks.st: and Jews found beneath it a heap of stones.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Check this pile.
chunks.st: Examine this heap of stones.

chunks.en: They checked it and found a statue in it.
chunks.st: And they examined it and found in it an idolatrous image.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to them:

chunks.en: Since it is the statue they worship,
chunks.st: Since it is the image that they worship,

chunks.en: we will allow them the tree.
chunks.st: we can permit use of the tree to those who wish to derive benefit from it.

summary: We may not sit in the shade of an ashera tree, or walk under it. The mishnah also says when we may plant vegetables under it.

chunks.en: He should not sit in its shade,
chunks.st: With regard to an ashera, one may not sit in its shade,

chunks.en: but if he sat there, he is tahor.
chunks.st: but if one sat in its shade he remains ritually pure.

chunks.en: And he should not walk under it.
chunks.st: And one may not pass beneath it,

chunks.en: If he walked under it, he is tamei.
chunks.explain: The tree is like a roof over him.
chunks.st: and if one passed beneath it he is ritually impure.

chunks.en: If its branches stole space from the public road,
chunks.st: If the tree was robbing the public, i.e., if its branches extended over public property,

chunks.en: and he walked under it, he is tahor.
chunks.st: and one passed beneath it, he remains pure.

chunks.en: We may plant vegetables under it in the rainy season,
chunks.explain: Then its shade does not help them grow.
chunks.st: One may plant vegetables underneath an ashera during the rainy season,
chunks.stMore: as the vegetables do not benefit from its shade; on the contrary, the tree’s foliage prevents the vegetables from being properly irrigated by the rain.

chunks.en: but not in the hot season.
chunks.st: But one may not plant vegetables under an ashera during the summer,
chunks.stMore: as the shade benefits them.

chunks.he: וְהַחֲזָרִין, לֹא בִימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
chunks.en: And lettuce — not in the hot season and not in the rainy season.
chunks.st: And lettuce may not be planted there at all, neither in the summer nor in the rainy season,
chunks.stMore: because shade is always beneficial to lettuce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: not even vegetables in the rainy season,
chunks.st: One may not plant vegetables under an ashera even during the rainy season,

chunks.en: because the leaves fall on them
chunks.st: because the tree’s foliage [shehaneviyya] falls upon them

chunks.en: and help them grow.
chunks.st: and serves as fertilizer for them.

summary: Wood from an ashera tree may not be used. Bread baked with it, or cloth woven with it, is forbidden, even if it gets mixed with others. Rabbi Eliezer has a different way to fix it.

chunks.en: If he took wood from it,
chunks.st: If one took wood from an ashera,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If he heated the oven with them,
chunks.st: In a case where one kindled a fire in an oven with the wood,

chunks.en: if it is new, it must be broken.
chunks.explain: The first fire makes a new oven stronger.
chunks.st: if it is a new oven and by kindling the fire he hardened the oven and made it stronger for use in the future, then the oven must be shattered.
chunks.stMore: Since forbidden items were used in the process of forming the oven, one may not derive benefit from the use of the forbidden items.

chunks.en: If it is old, it must cool off.
chunks.st: But if it is an old oven it may be cooled;
chunks.stMore: it is prohibited to use the oven only while it is still hot.

chunks.en: If he baked bread in it,
chunks.st: If one baked bread with wood from the ashera as the fuel,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from the bread.

chunks.en: If it got mixed with other loaves,
chunks.st: If this bread was intermingled with other bread,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from any of them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from all the bread.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he takes the benefit to the Dead Sea.
chunks.explain: He throws away money worth the wood he used.
chunks.st: One must take the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea.
chunks.stMore: In other words, one is not required to destroy all of the loaves. Instead, one should designate money equal in value to the wood that he used from the ashera, and he should destroy this money to offset the benefit he derived from the forbidden wood.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Avodah zarah cannot be redeemed with money.
chunks.st: There is no monetary redemption for objects that are forbidden due to idol worship.
chunks.stMore: Once the bread becomes forbidden, it cannot be redeemed by having the value of the forbidden wood cast into the Dead Sea.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: If he took a weaving tool from it,
chunks.st: If one took wood from an ashera for use as a weaving shuttle [karkor],

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If he wove the cloth with it,
chunks.st: If one wove a garment with it,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from the cloth.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from the garment.

chunks.en: If it got mixed with others, and others with others,
chunks.st: If the garment was intermingled with other garments, and those other garments were intermingled with others,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from any of them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from all of them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he takes the benefit to the Dead Sea.
chunks.st: One must take the benefit and cast it into the Dead Sea.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: Avodah zarah cannot be redeemed with money.
chunks.st: There is no monetary redemption for objects that are forbidden due to idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

summary: How does a non-Jew make an ashera tree stop being an idol? If he cuts off even a leaf for his own use, it is no longer an idol.

chunks.en: How does he cancel it?
chunks.st: How does one revoke the idolatrous status of an ashera?

chunks.en: If he cut off dry branches or green twigs for himself,
chunks.st: If a gentile trimmed dry wood or pruned green wood from the tree for his own benefit,

chunks.en: or took a stick or a branch from it,
chunks.st: or if he removed from it a stick, or a rod,

chunks.en: even a leaf,
chunks.st: or even a leaf,

chunks.en: it is canceled.
chunks.explain: This shows he no longer worships it.
chunks.st: he has thereby revoked
chunks.stMore: its idolatrous status, as he has proven that he no longer worships it.

chunks.en: If he trimmed it to make it look nice, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: If a gentile shaved down the tree for its own sake, to improve its appearance, it remains prohibited to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: If not to make it look nice, it is allowed.
chunks.st: If he shaved it down not for its own sake, it is permitted.
